cases.sentence: Графиня уже одетая по дорожному, в шали и шляпе, усталая, ходила но гостиной, ожидая домашних с тем, чтобы посидеть с ___ и помолиться перед отъездом.
cases.explain: «закрытыми дверями» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Sónya jumped out of the coach and ran to the countess. The countess, tired out and already dressed in shawl and bonnet for her journey, was pacing up and down the drawing room, waiting for the household to assemble for the usual silent prayer with closed doors before starting. Natásha was not in the room.

cases.sentence: Корректура страницы 74-й ___ первого издания «Войны и мира» 1868—1869 гг.
cases.explain: «пятого тома» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “The ways of God are past finding out!” she thought, feeling that the Almighty Hand, hitherto unseen, was becoming manifest in all that was now taking place.

cases.explain: «печатному виду» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Nothing,” answered the countess. “If everything is ready let us start.”

cases.explain: «семейным преданиям» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: (The most precious ones, with which some family tradition was connected, were being taken with them.)

cases.sentence: ___ Ефим, с которым одним только решалась ездить графиня, сидя высоко на своих козлах, даже не оглядывался на то, чтò делалось позади его.
cases.explain: «Старый кучер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Efím, the old coachman, who was the only one the countess trusted to drive her, sat perched up high on the box and did not so much as glance round at what was going on behind him. From thirty years’ experience he knew it would be some time yet before the order, “Be off, in God’s name!” would be given him: and he knew that even when it was said he would be stopped once or twice more while they sent back to fetch something that had been forgotten, and even after that he would again be stopped and the countess herself would lean out of the window and beg him for the love of heaven to drive carefully down the hill. He knew all this and therefore waited calmly for what would happen, with more patience than the horses, especially the near one, the chestnut Falcon, who was pawing the ground and champing his bit. At last all were seated, the carriage steps were folded and pulled up, the door was shut, somebody was sent for a traveling case, and the countess leaned out and said what she had to say. Then Efím deliberately doffed his hat and began crossing himself. The postilion and all the other servants did the same. “Off, in God’s name!” said Efím, putting on his hat. “Start!” The postilion started the horses, the off pole horse tugged at his collar, the high springs creaked, and the body of the coach swayed. The footman sprang onto the box of the moving coach which jolted as it passed out of the yard onto the uneven roadway; the other vehicles jolted in their turn, and the procession of carriages moved up the street. In the carriages, the calèche, and the phaeton, all crossed themselves as they passed the church opposite the house. Those who were to remain in Moscow walked on either side of the vehicles seeing the travelers off.

cases.sentence: Она изредка высовывалась в окно кареты и глядела назад и вперед на ___ раненых, предшествующий им.
cases.explain: «длинный поезд» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Rarely had Natásha experienced so joyful a feeling as now, sitting in the carriage beside the countess and gazing at the slowly receding walls of forsaken, agitated Moscow. Occasionally she leaned out of the carriage window and looked back and then forward at the long train of wounded in front of them. Almost at the head of the line she could see the raised hood of Prince Andréy’s calèche. She did not know who was in it, but each time she looked at the procession her eyes sought that calèche. She knew it was right in front.

cases.sentence: — Ей Богу, Безухов, в кафтане, с каким-то ___.
cases.explain: «старым мальчиком» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Yes, it really is Bezúkhov in a coachman’s coat, with a queer-looking old boy. Really,” said Natásha, “look, look!”

cases.sentence: Наконец, когда он понял его, посмотрел по указанию и, узнав Наташу, в ту же секунду, отдаваясь ___, быстро направился к карете.
cases.explain: «первому впечатлению» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: In fact, however, though now much farther off than before, the Rostóvs all saw Pierre—or someone extraordinarily like him—in a coachman’s coat, going down the street with head bent and a serious face beside a small, beardless old man who looked like a footman. That old man noticed a face thrust out of the carriage window gazing at them, and respectfully touching Pierre’s elbow said something to him and pointed to the carriage. Pierre, evidently engrossed in thought, could not at first understand him. At length when he had understood and looked in the direction the old man indicated, he recognized Natásha, and following his first impulse stepped instantly and rapidly toward the coach. But having taken a dozen steps he seemed to remember something and stopped.

cases.explain: «ужасное время» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Oh, don’t ask me, don’t ask me! I don’t know myself. Tomorrow … But no! Goodbye, goodbye!” he muttered. “It’s an awful time!” and dropping behind the carriage he stepped onto the pavement.
